title: Checks it, then asks Riley
does: A question the booking answers, like the time or the address, is answered at once. Otherwise Riley gets the words, with quick answers to tap.
more: No answer in 10 minutes: it goes to Sam, and the customer hears the shop was asked.
A question that can wait, sent at night, waits for the morning. The customer is told, and Sam is texted at 8am.
A question only a pro may answer gets the shop's line: 'Riley will go over it at your visit.'
A question nobody here may answer, like a legal one, gets: 'We can't advise on legal questions; a lawyer can help.'
Never promise it for the visit.
The plug-in's urgent words, like labor or water breaking, ring the on-call person at once, any hour.
Never: answer urgent words with 'it waits for the morning'. Staff never quote prices by text.
Words that hold something private reach Riley as 'Read it on the secure page'.
A report that someone at the business harmed a person goes to Rosie's team that day.
It never goes to the one named (judgment rule 58).
Abuse aimed at Riley is never passed on. Sam hears what kind came, and decides about the booking.
Safe default: it goes to Sam; nothing changes.
